recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Do not edit the orphaned source/familymemberhistory/valueset-birth-sex.xml file for FHIR-17561; if maintainers want to remove or normalize stale terminology source, handle that as separate build-system cleanup. Revisit FamilyMemberHistory.sex only when FHIR-55021 or another later sex/gender decision reaches Applied/Published status.
issue_request: FHIR-17561 was a Published Patient Care STU3 change request with a Persuasive with Modification resolution. It asked to update the old FamilyMemberHistory.gender definition to "The birth sex of the family member.", create an extensible Birth Sex value set from AdministrativeGender with male, female, and unknown while excluding other, and leave the existing requirements unchanged.
initial_application: Historical commit d073d22f6c applied GF#17561 by changing the old spreadsheet-era FamilyMemberHistory.gender source to a CodeableConcept with the birth-sex definition and an extensible new Birth Sex value set. The current source lineage now exposes the renamed FamilyMemberHistory.sex element with the requested birth-sex definition and an extensible CodeableConcept binding.
additional_context: Later published Patient Care decisions changed how the binding portion of FHIR-17561 should be interpreted. FHIR-17564 rejected a birthSex rename because reported family-member information can be imprecise; FHIR-17780 later renamed the element from gender to sex and updated the sex-oriented comment/requirements. FHIR-18850 intentionally changed the binding from the Birth Sex value set to AdministrativeGender, and FHIR-18848, FHIR-19716, and FHIR-43360 reaffirmed keeping the administrative-gender terminology family, including other, rather than restoring the original Birth Sex exclusion. FHIR-20393 later corrected the binding URL to the canonical AdministrativeGender value set URL. FHIR-55021 may revise the element for R6, but it is only Resolved - change required and is not Applied/Published in this run scope.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/fhir.ini lists FamilyMemberHistory as an active resource, and source/familymemberhistory/structuredefinition-FamilyMemberHistory.xml defines FamilyMemberHistory.sex as "The birth sex of the family member." with an extensible AdministrativeGender binding. Restoring the old Birth Sex value set or excluding administrative-gender#other would contradict later final decisions in the same FamilyMemberHistory issue family.
